title: Russian cipher telegrams seized by the Xinjiang governor, sent to Beijing to be deciphered
correspondents: Russian officials in Xinjiang (unknown) → unknown; forwarded by Ministry of Finance → Waijiaobu
shelfmark: Academia Sinica IMH Archives, Waijiaobu (外交部) files, 財政部「鈔送新疆省長所扣俄人密電請譯出見復由」(館藏號 not shown in the union-catalogue snippet)
folio_note: 4 pp., original (原檔); the title asks the Foreign Ministry to translate/decipher the seized telegrams, i.e. they reached Beijing undeciphered
status: Catalogue title: copies of Russians' cipher telegrams held by the Xinjiang governor, "please decipher and reply". Whether a reading was ever returned is not known. Not on DECODE.
why: Russian (White or Soviet) cipher traffic from Xinjiang in 1920, the year the White remnants fled into Chinese Turkestan; a rare Chinese intercept of Russian ciphertext.

title: Russian officers' and Kashgar consul's cipher telegrams detained in Xinjiang
correspondents: Russian army officers and the Russian consul at Kashgar → unknown; Xinjiang governor Yang Zengxin → Waijiaobu
shelfmark: Academia Sinica IMH Archives, Waijiaobu 03-32 (俄國, 新疆) series: 新疆省長「俄軍官密電應否扣留等事」(7 pp.); 03-32-108-04-014/-015 (扣留新省俄軍官往來密碼事, 抄送電稿); 03-32-108-04-024 (駐喀什俄領拍發密電事); 03-32-116 (參陸辦公處); 俄使館「據駐喀什領事報稱華官扣留密電稿報事」(3 pp.)

why: Japanese army traffic during the Siberian Intervention and the 1920 Nikolaevsk aftermath as seen by Chinese intelligence.
